title: Naturality of iterated local Frobenius for morphisms of constructible Weil pairs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb/\Ql$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$, with geometric Frobenius as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. All coefficient categories are the raw rationalized constructible categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and Weil pairs and their morphisms are those of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the specified natural pullback-composition and pullback/scalar comparisons, rationalized with their equality-of-morphisms and finite-iteration compatibilities, of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

Let $F/\Ql$ be finite inside $\Qlb$, let $n\geq1$, and let $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ with its specified geometric point $\bar x:s\to X$. Write $P=L\bar x_F^*$, $Q=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,F}$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $D=QP$, $G_r=L(g_X^r)_F^*$ and $S_r=L(g_s^r)_F^*$ for $r\geq1$. For a constructible point complex $N$, let $I_N^{[r]}:Q(N)\to Q(S_rN)$ be the $r$-fold point transport in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], using $\iota$ of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. Let
$$\rho_M:S_nP(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}PG_n(M),\qquad R(M)=Q(\rho_M)I_{P(M)}^{[n]}:D(M)\to D(G_nM),$$
where $\rho$ is the specified return comparison for $g_X^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$.

The following naturality assertions hold on the full constructible domain. For every morphism $w:N\to N'$ in $D^b_c(s,F)$ and $r\geq1$,
$$Q(S_rw)I_N^{[r]}=I_{N'}^{[r]}Q(w).$$
For every morphism $v:M\to M'$ in $D^b_c(X,F)$,
$$PG_n(v)\rho_M=\rho_{M'}S_nP(v),\qquad D(G_nv)R(M)=R(M')D(v).$$
For any two $F$-Weil pairs $(A,\alpha),(B,\beta)$ and any morphism of pairs $v:(A,\alpha)\to(B,\beta)$, so $v\alpha=\beta G_1(v)$, their specified iterated structure maps satisfy
$$v\alpha^{[r]}=\beta^{[r]}G_r(v)\quad(r\geq1).$$
Consequently their local operators $\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(A,\alpha)=D(\alpha^{[n]})R(A)$ and $\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(B,\beta)=D(\beta^{[n]})R(B)$ satisfy
$$D(v)\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(A,\alpha)=\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(B,\beta)D(v).$$
The morphism $v$ need not be invertible. No integral Weil-stable lattice or finite-reduction Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
Work at the fixed finite field extension $F/\Ql$. By clause 3 of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $Q$ is a functor on the raw rationalized point category. Put $T=S_1$. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural], with $E=F$ and $\Lambda=F$, gives, for every morphism $w:N\to N'$ in that category,
$$Q(Tw)\iota_N=\iota_{N'}Q(w).$$
This assertion already applies to every rational constructible morphism; it is not restricted to integral maps. In particular it applies to $T^j(w)$ for each $j\geq0$.

source.place: Displayed alternating-trace formula; agent-supplied starting naturality square for its local operator.

proof.text:
We prove naturality of the iterated point transport by induction, including its specified composition comparison. Set $J_{1,N}=\iota_N$ and $J_{r+1,N}=\iota_{T^rN}J_{r,N}$, so $J_{r,N}:Q(N)\to Q(T^rN)$. The base $Q(Tw)J_{1,N}=J_{1,N'}Q(w)$ is step 1. If $Q(T^rw)J_{r,N}=J_{r,N'}Q(w)$, then step 1 applied to $T^rw$, followed by the induction hypothesis, gives
$$Q(T^{r+1}w)J_{r+1,N}
=\iota_{T^rN'}Q(T^rw)J_{r,N}
=J_{r+1,N'}Q(w).$$
Let $c_r:S_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$ be the iterated pullback-composition comparison. By [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] its rationalization is natural and respects finite iterations. The definition in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] is exactly $I_N^{[r]}=Q(c_{r,N}^{-1})J_{r,N}$. Naturality of $c_r^{-1}$ now gives
$$Q(S_rw)I_N^{[r]}=Q(c_{r,N'}^{-1})Q(T^rw)J_{r,N}=I_{N'}^{[r]}Q(w).$$
Thus the induction proves the first asserted equation for every positive $r$.

source.place: Displayed alternating-trace formula; agent-supplied induction for the point-transport factor in local Frobenius.

proof.text:
Write $H=L(g_X^n\bar x)^*_F=L(\bar xg_s^n)^*_F$, where the equality is precisely the return equality stipulated in the statement. The specified comparisons give natural isomorphisms $a:H\xrightarrow{\sim}S_nP$ and $b:H\xrightarrow{\sim}PG_n$. Indeed these are the two composition comparisons in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], whose rationalizations respect equality of scheme morphisms. Consequently the specified return map is $\rho_M=b_Ma_M^{-1}$, not a newly chosen isomorphism. For $v:M\to M'$, the two naturality squares give
$$PG_n(v)b_M=b_{M'}H(v),\qquad H(v)a_M^{-1}=a_{M'}^{-1}S_nP(v).$$
Multiplying these equations yields $PG_n(v)\rho_M=\rho_{M'}S_nP(v)$, which is the asserted return-comparison naturality. We used $g_X^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$, and did not replace it by the generally false equality $g_X^n\bar x=\bar x$.

source.place: Displayed alternating-trace formula; agent-supplied calculation for the semilinear geometric-point return.

proof.text:
Apply $Q$ to step 3 and use step 2 with $w=P(v)$ and $r=n$. Functoriality, the definition $R(M)=Q(\rho_M)I_{P(M)}^{[n]}$, and these two equations give
$$\begin{aligned}
D(G_nv)R(M)&=Q(PG_n(v))Q(\rho_M)I_{P(M)}^{[n]}\\
&=Q(\rho_{M'})Q(S_nP(v))I_{P(M)}^{[n]}\\
&=Q(\rho_{M'})I_{P(M')}^{[n]}Q(P(v))=R(M')D(v).
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the asserted naturality of $R$ for every underlying morphism $v$.

source.place: Displayed alternating-trace formula; agent-supplied multiplication of the point-transport and return squares.

proof.text:
For the Weil-pair morphism $v$, [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] gives $v\alpha=\beta G_1(v)$. This is the base $r=1$ of the desired induction. Let $k_r:G_{r+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_rG_1$ be the specified natural composition comparison of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. The recursion of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], with comparisons written in, is $\alpha^{[r+1]}=\alpha^{[r]}G_r(\alpha)k_{r,A}$ and likewise for $\beta$. Assume $v\alpha^{[r]}=\beta^{[r]}G_r(v)$. Then
$$\begin{aligned}
v\alpha^{[r+1]}&=\beta^{[r]}G_r(v)G_r(\alpha)k_{r,A}\\
&=\beta^{[r]}G_r(\beta)G_rG_1(v)k_{r,A}\\
&=\beta^{[r]}G_r(\beta)k_{r,B}G_{r+1}(v)
=\beta^{[r+1]}G_{r+1}(v).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equalities use functoriality and the one-step intertwining equation, then naturality of $k_r$. This proves the asserted intertwining for all $r\geq1$.

source.place: Displayed alternating-trace formula; agent-supplied induction on its iterated Weil-structure factor.

proof.text:
Finally apply the functor $D$ to the equality of step 5 at $r=n$, and multiply by $R(A)$. Step 4 applied to the underlying map of the Weil-pair morphism gives
$$\begin{aligned}
D(v)\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(A,\alpha)
&=D(v)D(\alpha^{[n]})R(A)\\
&=D(\beta^{[n]})D(G_nv)R(A)\\
&=D(\beta^{[n]})R(B)D(v)
=\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(B,\beta)D(v).
\end{aligned}$$
These are the local operators of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. No inverse of $v$ was used in any step. Every equality was obtained in the full rational constructible categories from the cited naturality and coherent-composition statements, so no Weil-stable integral lattice or condition on the Tor amplitude of finite reductions is needed.

The item was created by Q128 when the parent lem-fd-local-weil-model-trace-independence was re-split; the re-split note is for that parent, not this item. The item is not on the dropped list. I read every cited statement in full. Step 1: clause 2 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural (Λ=E) and clause 3 of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point give one-step naturality of ι at the rational level. Step 2: the induction J_{r+1}=ι_{T^rN}J_r has a stated base and step; I = Q(c_r^{-1})J_r, where c_r is the iterated natural c^E of lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization, and the direction F_{kh}→F_hF_k checks. Step 3: a=c_{g_s^n,x̄} and b=c_{x̄,g_X^n} share the source H by the return equality g^n x̄=x̄ g_s^n (which the trf node's 'respect equality of scheme morphisms' covers), so ρ=ba^{-1}: S_nP→PG_n is the definition's middle isomorphism. Step 4: three-line calculation with Q. Step 5: the recursion α^{[r+1]}=α^{[r]}G_r(α)k_{r,A} with k_r=c_{g^r,g}; the induction goes through the IH, the base square and naturality of k_r, and never inverts v. Step 6 checked. Edge cases checked: n=r=1, X_0=Spec k_0, v=0, a noninvertible v between Jordan blocks, period dividing n. Overlaps: lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle (strict finite coefficients, a cocycle identity) and lem-trf-frobenius-transport-induction (two forms of the transport) are not duplicates. Advisory: the first clause of lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization already states naturality of t_{y,m} at E, which is essentially the item's R-naturality; the item has further clauses, so it is not a duplicate.
